source: WebMCP Draft Community Group Report, 8 October 2026 (https://webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp/): ToolAnnotations has exactly readOnlyHint, untrustedContentHint, consequentialHint and debugging.
description: WebMCP annotations are derived from catalog fields, never authored. Rule forms: copy:<field>, not-equal:<field>:<value> in:<field>:<value>,<value>... and any:<field>,<field>... (true when any listed boolean field is true), where field is annotations.readOnlyHint, confirmation, returnsUntrustedContent, contentEgress, peerSupplied (the tool lists peerSuppliedFields) or group.diagnostic. The Go validator and the mcp/webmcp generator interpret the same rules.

notes.exposed: Not a WebMCP annotation: whether the tool is registered in the browser at all. An allow-list (R13 security L7): only none and write tools are registered; destructive tools, and any confirmation class added later, are never registered through WebMCP unless this rule names them (webmcp-tool-package). An unknown class is an error, not a default.
notes.dropped: destructiveHint, idempotentHint and openWorldHint are not defined by the WebMCP draft and are not emitted.
